This nation’s failure to address its gun violence crisis is a sin that will never be forgiven. And how could it ever be? For decades, Americans have gone from one day to the next standing on the brink of another tragedy. Yet there has been no action, no progress, no change — just more broken communities, and more unbearable grief. Enough.

My prayers are with the people of Erie and the families of all the victims of this most painful moment. They deserve justice, and a country that is decent enough to deliver it.

For nearly two long and painful years, Americans have watched in helpless horror as our neighbors continue to be stolen from their homes and shot in the street by agents of the Trump Administration. Last night’s attempted murder of a New Yorker in front of his five-year-old son was far from the first disgraceful incident of its kind, but it must be the last. We demand that ICE leave our city immediately, and we are too disgusted to accept any delay.

While the Trump Administration’s government-sanctioned abuses have shocked our collective conscience and sickened our society, we cannot say that we are surprised to see them befall our communities. I fought bitterly to prevent Donald Trump and his congressional lackeys from empowering ICE with hundreds of billions in taxpayer dollars, because I was certain that these vile, unconstitutional crimes were an inevitability under this president’s watch. 

In fact, these depravities are the only promise Donald Trump has kept, serving as more red meat for his MAGA followers. Every incident is just another dreadful reminder of the resources that could have been spent positioning our society towards a brighter future. Not pulling the darkest chapters of our past back to the present.

ICE has proven itself nothing more than a vigilante weapon for the white nationalists to tear away at our multiracial democracy. It is a rogue agency, built by and for broken men. The only path forward is to rip that power away entirely, before ICE has any opportunity to further its relentless escalation of violence and despair in America. 

I therefore call upon Secretary Mullin to immediately remove ICE from sanctuary cities like New York City and all others his agents have invaded. The choice is his – however, the power is ours. Go out and vote!

ICE brings despair and violence to every city its agents invade. New York will not be safe as long as a single one of these cruel thugs remains in our communities, and we will not have justice until all those who nearly murdered a New Yorker and his child are prosecuted for their sick crime.

We demand ICE gets out, and stays out. Immediately.

When America’s adversaries abroad target our elections by spreading disinformation, sowing distrust, and striking at our election-security infrastructure, we expect our president to stand up to their attacks on free and fair elections – not start his own. The Trump Administration’s shameful betrayal of our democracy has long been in the works, and it’s only grown more dangerous in the era of AI. I’ve been sounding the alarm for years.

I introduced the REAL Political Ads Act to end the tide of undisclosed AI-generated political ads muddying our elections, and I led the DEEPFAKES Accountability Act to combat malicious deepfakes and foreign election interference. Democracy depends on people staying informed. Trump’s power rests on people being deceived. 

https://t.co/JvYKWEMN9n

Today marks three painful years past the October 7th terrorist attack on Israel, when Hamas murdered more than 1,200 men, women, and children and abducted 251 others into brutal captivity. My heart and thoughts are with the countless families who have suffered an unthinkable, unbearable grief that came with that terrible day and will stay with them forever.

The vile tide of antisemitism and islamophobia that arrived in the October 7th attack’s aftermath has been felt by innocents throughout our world, including far too many of our Jewish and Muslim neighbors across Brooklyn. In the name of all those we have lost, and all others we hope to save, we must continue to stand against hatred in all its forms. The work of building a future where our coexistence is accepted as a source of strength, and not seen as an excuse to divide, must go on.

We can create a world where all are welcome, and safe, and loved – but only if we try.

Like countless Americans, I know the fear, heartbreak, and uncertainty that follows a prostate cancer diagnosis devastatingly well – I felt it myself when my own father received his diagnosis. As we mark the end of this Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, and as countless families across America struggle to face such an unbearable pain, we must recommit to building a nation where no family ever does again. I introduced the PSA Screening for Him Act to make prostate cancer screenings more accessible by waiving deductibles, copayments, and coinsurances for certain individuals at high risk of developing prostate cancer, because defeating this disease starts with detecting it.

Systemic injustice does not occur spontaneously. It is born in the cruel and controlling hearts of politicians who steal our power and pretend it is their own. As Members of Congress, we have a moral responsibility to stop the Hyde Amendment before it reaches one more year and harms any more women. Now is the time we come together to put an end to this vicious chapter in our history. That starts with passing the EACH Act and ensuring that every American can access affordable abortion care, no matter what.

While there is no shortage of cruelties lurking in the laws of this nation, the Hyde Amendment is particularly sickening because its negative impacts are felt mostly by those with the least. For half a century, it has blocked low-income Americans from having access to insurance when seeking abortion coverage. For Black and brown women, as well as those belonging to rural communities who have long navigated systemic discrimination and contended with trauma and hardship in their struggle to receive care, its impact and consequences have been especially devastating.

posts.text: Today marks 50 years of harm, hardship, and uncertainty under the Hyde Amendment. Since its adoption in 1976, the Hyde Amendment has relentlessly and brutally restricted a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions. Its vile legacy can be seen in the countless women it has affected over this painful past century, as well as in every regression in this nation that its very existence has made possible. Indeed, the Supreme Court’s decision to overturn Roe v. Wade and deny millions of women their right to an abortion could only have arrived in the wake of a post-Hyde America, where women’s autonomy has remained under siege, and our personal medical decisions are offered to all hands but our own.

We cannot say exactly what they schemed, today. But I am certain we'll see the consequences soon enough.

On behalf of the people of the 9th District of New York, the Clarke family, and myself, I wish to extend my heartfelt condolences to the many loved ones and countless fellow fans of the internationally renowned Mr. Slinger Francisco, the Mighty Sparrow, as we grieve this peerless icon’s transition to paradise. Though he was born in Grenada and raised in Trinidad and Tobago, the Mighty Sparrow’s talent was so substantial and his art so impactful, it could not be confined to the nations of the Caribbean, but instead came to be beloved across the globe. Indeed, the “Calypso King of the World” earned his crown through his remarkable talent, generous spirit, and unrelenting commitment to his craft. I have no doubt that incomparable legacy will persist long past the loss of our Legend. We will remember the Mighty Sparrow as a consummate entertainer, celebrate him as a cultural institution, and honor him as the trailblazer, charitable soul, and innovator he was. And, though our sorrow is great, may we find comfort in knowing that tonight, the Kingdom of Heaven will ring alive with sweet steel melodies and the songs and sounds of our people.

I commend @NewYorkStateAG for recognizing the real danger of unregulated AI.

Democrats have been sounding the alarm: 
AI is advancing faster than the guardrails meant to protect our privacy, civil rights, consumers, and communities can keep up, and it’s clear Big Tech cannot be left to police itself.

Congress has a responsibility to provide real oversight, transparency, and accountability here. Innovation without oversight is not progress; it's a risk, and Congress must act.

https://t.co/hf0gDxkSfh
